# Scribl D2C AWS Estimate V3

_Source artifact: `s2d/inputs/scribl-d2c-aws-estimate-v3.xlsx`. Generated by context-ingest; do not hand-edit._

## README

| Scribl D2C  -  Infrastructure TCO Model |   |   |   |   |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| What this is |   |   |   |   |
| A 30-month run-rate model (Oct 2026 - Mar 2029) for Scribl D2C infrastructure, built bottom-up from the six |   |   |   |   |
| consumption pillars: Compute (EKS), Security (Cognito + WAF), Networking (ALB + data transfer), |   |   |   |   |
| Database (DynamoDB + Aurora), Storage (S3), and AI App (Bedrock + Claude). A Data Lake / ML research |   |   |   |   |
| workstream switches on after Year 1 for mental-health outcomes research and dataset publishing. Unit prices |   |   |   |   |
| are anchored to AWS us-east-2 (Ohio) and Anthropic rates, both validated June 2026. |   |   |   |   |
| Drivers of consumption |   |   |   |   |
| Pillars are listed largest first. AI Inference is the dominant line, around 60% of the 30-month total and |   |   |   |   |
| about two-thirds at full scale. The rest is real infrastructure: the model runs three environments (dev, |   |   |   |   |
| stage, prod), so compute and database carry an always-on baseline. The gross floor is around $11k/month at |   |   |   |   |
| launch; roughly $9.5k is demand-driven and the remainder is reserved launch-readiness headroom you can dial |   |   |   |   |
| on the Assumptions tab. User scaling and regional expansion lift it from there. |   |   |   |   |
| AI Inference  (Bedrock + Claude) |   |   |   |   |
| The daily prompt is generated once for all users, so prompt generation runs about 150 calls a month and |   |   |   |   |
| costs roughly five dollars. The rest is per-item: a vision read on every drawing that returns a caption or |   |   |   |   |
| headline, and a moderation check on every submission. The calls Claude makes inside the product: |   |   |   |   |
| Inference feature | Model | Fires on | Calls/mo @ 5M | Share of AI $ |
| Daily prompt generation | Opus 4.8 | Once per day, all users | ~150 | <0.1% |
| Drawing read + caption/headline | Sonnet 4.6 (vision) | Every drawing submitted | ~14.6M | ~78% |
| Content moderation | Haiku 4.5 | Every submission | ~26.6M | ~22% |
| Personalized follow-ups | Agentic (memory) | Post-launch; not modelled | -- | -- |
| Exciting Artifact composition | Generative | Q1 2027; not modelled | -- | -- |
| Shares are at default assumptions and 5M users. The two post-launch features are listed for completeness; |   |   |   |   |
| neither is in the cost numbers. |   |   |   |   |
| Compute  (EKS) |   |   |   |   |
| One EKS cluster per environment runs the application services. Production runs in every active region while |   |   |   |   |
| dev and stage stay in the primary region, so the cluster count goes from three today (dev, stage, prod in |   |   |   |   |
| Ohio) to five at full three-region expansion (prod in all three regions, plus dev and stage in Ohio). The |   |   |   |   |
| Drivers tab shows this count, and control plane, load balancers, NAT, and WAF all scale with it. Production |   |   |   |   |
| worker nodes scale with DAU from a four-node HA floor (m5.xlarge, us-east-2, 25% Savings Plan), with dev and |   |   |   |   |
| stage at half. Observability (CloudWatch, Prometheus, Grafana, X-Ray) has a fixed base per environment plus a variable component |   |   |   |   |
| that grows with API traffic. The platform baseline (ECR, Secrets, CI, bastion) stays fixed. An explicit |   |   |   |   |
| reserved/standby line sets how much launch-readiness and DR headroom you hold ahead of demand. |   |   |   |   |
| Security  (Cognito + WAF) |   |   |   |   |
| Cognito is billed on monthly active users using AWS volume tiers (first 50,000 free, then a declining rate |   |   |   |   |
| from $0.0055 down to $0.0025 per MAU), so it tracks the MAU line and becomes the largest non-AI line at five |   |   |   |   |
| million users. WAF runs a web ACL per environment plus a per-request inspection fee. Both price the same |   |   |   |   |
| across regions, so this pillar carries no regional premium. |   |   |   |   |
| Networking  (ALB + data transfer) |   |   |   |   |
| Load balancers and NAT gateways run per environment per region, a fixed baseline that grows as regions come |   |   |   |   |
| online. The variable half is outbound data transfer from channel browsing, which becomes the largest |   |   |   |   |
| networking line at scale; the 'media views per DAU per day' input moves it most, and Singapore egress is the |   |   |   |   |
| priciest of the three regions. Media delivery does not route through NAT. |   |   |   |   |
| Database  (DynamoDB + Aurora) |   |   |   |   |
| Aurora Serverless v2 is the relational system of record; production ACUs scale with DAU above a ten-ACU HA |   |   |   |   |
| floor, while dev and stage scale to a low idle floor as Serverless v2 is designed to. ElastiCache (Redis) |   |   |   |   |
| and OpenSearch (search plus log analytics) run as always-on baselines across all environments. DynamoDB |   |   |   |   |
| carries high-velocity items on-demand and stays small. Aurora plus the cache and search baselines make this |   |   |   |   |
| the second-largest floor at launch. |   |   |   |   |
| Storage  (S3) |   |   |   |   |
| Cumulative media: every drawing, voice clip, and text response is kept, so the line only climbs, even if |   |   |   |   |
| DAU flattens. The model uses an effective rate that blends S3 Standard ($0.023/GB in us-east-2) with |   |   |   |   |
| lifecycle tiering of aged media to Infrequent Access. Request charges (PUT on submit, GET on view) are a |   |   |   |   |
| second, smaller component. |   |   |   |   |
| Data Lake / ML research |   |   |   |   |
| Centralized in the primary region (us-east-2), not replicated regionally. Lake storage grows with the user |   |   |   |   |
| base; cost also tracks researcher headcount through SageMaker notebooks and Athena query scan, plus GPU |   |   |   |   |
| hours for model training. The workstream is gated to start in the month set on the Assumptions tab (default |   |   |   |   |
| month 13). The compute is modest; the consent and de-identification work behind it is not, and sits outside |   |   |   |   |
| this model. |   |   |   |   |
| Regional deployment |   |   |   |   |
| The model launches in us-east-2 (Ohio) and expands production to two more regions. Each one adds cost two |   |   |   |   |
| ways: a duplicated production footprint (an extra cluster, load balancers, NAT, and WAF) and a price premium |   |   |   |   |
| on the traffic served there. Dev and stage stay in Ohio. Start months and premiums are editable on the |   |   |   |   |
| Assumptions tab. |   |   |   |   |
| Region | Role | Live from | Premium vs Ohio |   |
| us-east-2 (Ohio) | Primary | Month 1 (launch) | baseline |   |
| eu-west-2 (London) | European expansion | Year 2 (month 13) | ~8% |   |
| ap-southeast-1 (Singapore) | Asian market | Year 2.5 (month 25) | ~18% |   |
| Premiums follow AWS regional pricing: London a few points above Ohio, Asia Pacific roughly 20-30% on compute |   |   |   |   |
| and higher on egress. Only the share of traffic in a region carries its premium, so the blended effect on |   |   |   |   |
| total cost is a few percent, not the headline premium. The research data lake stays in Ohio and is not |   |   |   |   |
| uplifted. |   |   |   |   |
